items.text: The United States Central Command says that the U.S. military has redirected seven commercial vehicles and disabled one since the blockade on Iranian ports was reinstated on July 14. ((Middle East Eye))

Greek shipping company Dynacom Tankers reports that two oil tankers, the Malta-flagged Panamax-sized tanker Kavomaleas and Liberian-flagged crude carrier Acheloos, were attacked off the coast of Oman near the Strait of Hormuz after being hit by unknown projectiles. ((Reuters))
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claims that two tankers have exploded after passing through the Strait of Hormuz. ((The Hill))
Mediators Pakistan and Qatar propose a 10-day ceasefire in an effort to revive the Islamabad Memorandum signed last month. ((MENA via The New Arab)) ((Reuters))
Iranian president Masoud Pezeshkian says that Iran is in a "full-scale war". ((The Guardian))
The Jordanian military says air defences intercepted three Iranian missiles targeting Jordan. ((AFP via Business Recorder))
The New York Times reports American soldiers were injured and several helicopters were damaged in Iranian strikes against Jordan. ((The Jerusalem Post)) ((The New York Times))
The Israeli military says that they have killed two Islamic Jihad militants in separate strikes in the Gaza Strip, in violation of the ongoing ceasefire. ((The Jerusalem Post))
Hamas names Khalil al-Hayya as its new leader, replacing former leader Yahya Sinwar. ((Reuters))

Houthi-controlled Yemen declares a maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia effective immediately, after accusing it of an "aggressive siege" against Yemen for nearly 12 years. ((Al Jazeera)) ((CNBC)) ((Reuters))
A plane operated by Saudi Arabia's King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Center arrives in Khartoum, Sudan, with aid, food, and medical supplies amidst the civil war. ((Asharq Al-Awsat))
The United States imposes new sanctions upon the Sudanese military junta, alleging the use of chemical weapons including chlorine gas in the civil war. ((RFI))
The Iraqi military say that they have destroyed six ISIS hideouts in Kirkuk, Iraq. ((Iraqi News))

U.S. president Donald Trump signs executive orders imposing 50% tariffs on many Canadian goods, including USMCA-covered products, citing discriminatory trade practices. The duties take effect in 30 days, with exemptions for energy, potash, and products under sector-specific tariffs. ((AFP via Vanguard)) ((CBC News))
The nationwide gas prices in the United States exceeds US$4 per gallon, the highest since June 17. ((AP)) ((NBC News))
Brent Crude oil surpasses US$90 per barrel as oil prices increase amidst the ongoing escalation, while West Texas Intermediate reaches $84.49. ((CNBC))
Twenty people are killed, 80 others are injured and more than 100 people remain missing after heavy rains caused flash floods in eastern Afghanistan. ((Xinhua))

A federal court in New York, U.S., sentences Sinaloa Cartel co-founder El Mayo to life imprisonment and orders $15 billion in forfeiture after he pled guilty to charges related to leading the cartel. ((AFP via Le Monde))
Heavy clashes erupts between police and protestors in Bologna, Italy, after 42-year-old Abderrahim Fakir was killed by police while being handcuffed the previous day. ((Il Sole 24 ore))

Indian riot police baton-charge protesters marching toward the Parliament House in New Delhi over irregularities involving the NEET. Thousands demand education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation, while Delhi Police restrict internet access and say the demonstration lacked permission. ((AFP via RFI))
Sir Keir Starmer resigns as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, and is succeeded by Andy Burnham. ((CNN)) ((The Guardian)) ((The Telegraph))
Santomean President Carlos Vila Nova wins a re-election with 55.94% of the vote, while his main opposition candidate Nito Abreu comes second with 41.42% of the vote ((Reuters))
Nicaraguan co-president Daniel Ortega announces that the country will hold no further elections in order to "build a wall" against the political opposition. ((The Guardian))
The Kuwaiti defense ministry reports that the military has intercepted ballistic missiles and drones entering Kuwait's airspace. ((Arab Times Kuwait))
The U.S. CENTCOM completes a 10th round of strikes against Iranian military command centers, missile and drone launch sites, maritime capabilities and air defense systems. ((Reuters))

U.S. president Donald Trump signs another executive order imposing 50% tariffs on many Canadian goods, including USMCA-covered products, citing alleged discriminatory trade practices. The duties take effect in 30 days, with exemptions for energy, potash, and products under sector-specific tariffs. ((AFP via Vanguard)) ((CBC News))

Heavy clashes erupt between police and protesters in Bologna, Italy, after a 42-year-old Moroccan man, Abderrahim Fakir, was killed by police while being handcuffed the previous day. ((Il Sole 24 ore)) ((Reuters))
Santomean president Carlos Vila Nova wins re-election with 55.94% of the vote, while his main opposition candidate Nito Abreu comes second with 41.42% of the vote. ((Reuters))

Twelve people are killed and 13 others are missing after a suspected methane explosion collapses part of a tunnel at a hydropower project along the Teesta River in Namchi, Sikkim, India. Rescue teams detect toxic gases while searching for those trapped. ((AFP via CNA))
Thounsands of fish die in a canal in Sint Maarten in what officials describe as the largest fish kill in the country's history. A critical drop in oxygen levels is being blamed for the deaths. ((AP))
Thousands of fish die in a canal in Sint Maarten in what officials describe as the largest fish kill in the country's history. A critical drop in oxygen levels is being blamed for the deaths. ((AP))
